text:
anya: heads up — saw a spike in resumed streaming sessions this morning that led to duplicated billing for a handful of tenants. rough logs attached below, only ~8 users but definite dup tokens.
anya: log snippet: `2026-03-18T09:12:02Z resume accepted token=rz-abc123 session=sz-9f1` then `2026-03-18T09:12:02Z new_session created session=sz-9f1 billing=charged`
anya: basically resume and new connect processed as separate billable requests. :confused:
infra-bot: deploy completed: rollout v2026.03.17.4 to streaming-proxy (canary) :rocket:
raf: ugh. this smells like a race in the proxy routing where resume path doesn't short-circuit quota check when session id already mapped.
raf: quick idea: treat resume as non-billable if the resume token is validated within X ms of the original session timeline. 
sam: we already have a 100ms sticky-routing window, but quota check happens before sticky update in code path A. ordering bug.
sam: patch would be to run resume token validation earlier and return a short-circuit response that marks request as resumed=true before quota billing call.
mike: careful — consoles and billing expect idempotency to be based on `Idempotency-Key`. we don't currently surface resume semantics in billing. if we short-circuit, billing may undercount some legitimate new sessions.
nieves: telemetry gap callout: console traces show session map updated ~30ms after resume acceptance, but billing logs show two charge events within 2ms. traces and logs misaligned. need correlated request id. :eyes:
anya: what if we add `X-Resume-Id` header on resume acceptance and propagate that to billing pipeline so charges with same resume id are deduped for N ms?
raf: yeah, `X-Resume-Id` + ephemeral dedupe in billing ingress sounds doable. also add a server-side check: if `session_id` already exists in the cache, drop the new charge.
sam: that requires consistent view across proxy instances. our session map is eventually consistent in cross-region setups. race still possible.
mike: maybe easier: introduce a 250ms billing grace window for requests that have `Resume-Token` present — i.e., delay billing event emission by 250ms and collapse duplicates by `session_id`/`resume_id`. Tradeoff: small billing latency.
nieves: we need console UX too — surface resumed=true in request logs and in per-route cost breakdown so customers can see resumed sessions not being double-billed. also expose a telemetry metric `streaming.resume.dedupe_rate`.
raf: rollout plan: feature-flag `resume-billing-dedupe`, enable in canary region for 24h, collect dedupe_rate, error rate, and token-mismatch rate.
anya: agreed. can we also add a short-term mitigation: log a high-severity alert when duplicate-charge for same session_id within 1s for >5 tenants in an hour?
mike: yes, add alert to billing-alerts with threshold. i'll owner.
sam: I'll open a small PR to reorder quota/resume validation (branch: platform/resume-shortcircuit). patch includes header propagation and metrics hooks.
raf: i'll spec the billing-side dedupe logic and `X-Resume-Id` contract (proto + cli example) and validate with sam's patch.
nieves: i'll wire up dash panels: per-region dedupe_rate, console tag `resumed` in request view, and a rollout chart for the FF.
infra-bot: ci pipeline: platform/resume-shortcircuit -> tests started (unit + integration).
anya: timeline: sam and raf to land changes behind FF by tomorrow EOD, canary for 48h, then expand. mike will monitor billing dedupe metrics and escalate if regressions.
raf: one more note — watch for edge-case where a stale resume token is replayed across regions; dedupe window must be bounded. propose 5s TTL.
sam: good call. will implement 5s dedupe TTL.
anya: thanks team. follow-ups in the PR and I've added the alert. :thumbsup:
